column1: # Call-count fingerprint groups: NAME <TAB> REGEX
# One regex per logical component, matched against the symbol names in BOTH engines'
# callgrind profiles and the matches summed. Each row is the claim "zfish calls this as
# often as Stockfish does" -- a claim about the ALGORITHM, not about cost, and immune to
# inlining as long as the symbol survives on both sides.
# WHAT THIS CATCHES THAT NOTHING ELSE HERE DOES. Every other differential in this tree
# compares VALUES -- the bench anchor, the UCI goldens, arch-determinism, upstream-walk --
# and each one passes over a state divergence that happens not to move a node count on the
# positions it drives. The sibling C port had two real defects living behind that all-green
# wall (a `ucinewgame` that discarded the position, and a mate/stalemate root that skipped
# the per-worker reset), and BOTH surfaced here as one call of difference in set_check_info.
# zfish reads 165,082 -- upstream's value, so it has neither -- but the check is what
# proves that rather than the reading of two files.
# CHOOSE SYMBOLS THAT SURVIVE INLINING ON BOTH SIDES. A group whose regex matches nothing
# on one side is a MISS and fails, because a silent zero would read as agreement forever.
# If a compiler change inlines a symbol away, fix the row rather than deleting the check,
# and prefer a callee too big to inline over its caller. `isDraw` has no row for exactly
# this reason: zfish inlines it away entirely, so there is nothing to compare.
# A THIRD FIELD SUBTRACTS. Some rows reach the same symbol through a path only ONE engine
# has, and then the row is comparing the harness rather than the component. The optional
# third field is a regex subtracted from that row on each side, so each engine nets out its
# OWN count -- never a hard-coded difference, which would rot the moment the bench list
# changed length. `set_check_info` is the case: see its row.
# NARROWING A ROW IS ALLOWED; SILENTLY SUMMING IS NOT. Where a compiler inlines one
# instantiation away on one side only, the row must not go on adding the surviving symbols
# against BOTH of the other side's -- that reads as a call-sequence divergence which is not
# there. Narrow both sides to the instantiation that survives on both, and NAME the half
# that is no longer covered, the way `isDraw` is named above. `threats` is that case.
# MATCH ONE SYMBOL PER SIDE, AND VERIFY IT. A loose regex silently sums symbols that are
# not the same thing: `Position::do_move` alone also catches upstream's delegating 4-arg
# overload (250 calls) and reads as a 250-call divergence that is not there. Check a new
# row with `perf_fingerprint.py calls <out> --match ...` before trusting it.
movepick
legal
gives_check
see_ge
# Upstream hands each worker its root by round-tripping the FEN -- `rootPos.set(pos.fen(), ..)`
# (thread.cpp) -- so every `go` costs an extra `Position::set` -> `set_state` ->
# `set_check_info`. zfish copies the Position struct and repoints `st` instead
# (platform/thread.zig), which is why its own comment records the bug that re-parsing
# caused. Same root, one fewer derivation: 103 setups against 52 at bench 16 1 8, and the
# row read 172,552 vs 172,501 for that reason alone. Subtracting each side's OWN setup
# count leaves the IN-SEARCH derivations, which is what this row is the canary for, and
# they agree exactly: 172,449 == 172,449 (do_move 170,508 + do_null_move 1,941).
set_check_info
do_move
undo_move
do_null_move
# zfish makes `put_piece` comptime where upstream leaves it a runtime bool, so zfish's TWO
# surviving symbols answer upstream's ONE `<true>` instantiation, and they sum to it exactly
# (303,078 == 303,078 at bench 16 1 8). The `compute_ray=false` pair reaches
# `updatePieceThreatsRays` directly and LLVM inlines it away entirely, so upstream's
# `<false>` (81,022) has nothing here to compare against -- the `isDraw` case above. The row
# used to sum zfish's two against upstream's two and report 0.789, which read as an
# algorithm divergence that was never there.
threats
# `applyCombinedDelta` still exists in nnue_acc_rowops.zig but LLVM inlines it away, so the
# old row matched NOTHING here and read 0 against upstream's 150,323. Retargeted at the
# callee that survives: `applyCombinedPsqtDelta` is called once beside it at both sites
# (nnue_acc_update.zig, nnue_acc_both.zig), so it fires exactly once per upstream
# `apply_combined` -- 150,323 == 150,323, verified per-symbol before this row was trusted.
acc_apply
acc_side
